name: Sarovar Bliss TRH Bhimtal
description: Bhimtal, another lake town adjoining the popular hill-station Nainital, is an idyllic vacation spot. Bhimtal is perfect for a serene holiday. With the arrival of migratory birds in winters, Bhimtal becomes a paradise for bird watchers. Legends say that Bhima, one of the Pandava from Mahabharata, created the picturesque lake.

name: TRH Abbott Mount (Gold Creast Eco log huts)
description: Situated at an elevation of around 1981M. above sea lavel in Champawat District, Abbott Mount is a picturesque hamlet. "It is said that a British businessman, John Harold Abbott, was so mesmerised by the serenity of this place that he decided to develop it as a European settlement" One can spot Himalayan Birds, colourful Butterflies and bright red Burans (Rhododendron) flowers, especially in summers. Nature walk Trekking, angling and photography can be enjoyed in this beautifull Hill station. Abbott Mount also offers clear view of The great Himalayan peaks that lie on the eastern side of the Kumaon Hills - a panorama that makes for a stunning photo opportunity.

name: Holiday Home Almora
description: The KMVN Tourist Rest house in Almora is strategically located on the Mall Road. It is a mid-range hotel best suited for budget travelers. The service of the Tourist Rest house is good and the rooms are provided with high quality basic amenities. Kumaon Mandal Vikas Nigam has been serving the tourists with value service ensuring a comfortable stay.
address: KMVN Holiday Home, Mall Road, Almora. (Uttarakhand) - 263601

name: TRH Baijnath
description: Baijnath is a small town on the banks of the Gomati river in the Bageshwar district in Kumaon division of Uttarakhand , India . The place is most noted for its ancient temples , [1] which have been recognized as Monuments of National Importance by the Archaeological Survey of India in Uttarakhand . Baijnath has been selected as one of the four places to be connected by the 'Shiva Heritage Circuit' in Kumaon , under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme of the Government of India .

name: TRH Bhowali
description: Just 11 Kms. away from Nainital, Bhowali is a beautiful hill station situated at an altitude of 1706 meters above the sea level, Bhowali provides some of the best of the views of the snow-capped mountains and lush green forests. Bhowali is famous for its local fruit market like apples, plums, peaches, strawberries and apricots. The incredible location of Bhowali, which is almost at the border of the Nainital, surrounded by several lakes, orchards, farms and tea estates is what makes it one of the best tourist destinations of the Kumaon region.

name: TRH Binsar (Nanda Devi TRH Binsar)
description: The forest gate, located approximately 10 km before TRH Binsar, operates daily from 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM in summer and from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM in winter. Please ensure that you enter before the closing time, as access through the gate is regulated by the Forest Department. Electricity will be available from the generator only for 3 hours in the dinner time. Geyser/Heater not available.

name: TRH Birthi
description: According to Census 2011 information the location code or village code of Birthi village is 048975. Birthi village is located in Munsiari tehsil of Pithoragarh district in Uttarakhand, India. It is situated 35km away from sub-district headquarter Munsiari (tehsildar office) and 88km away from district headquarter Pithoragarh. As per 2009 stats, Bhurting is the gram panchayat of Birthi village.

name: TRH Champawat
description: Champawat is believed to be the place where the Kurmavtar (the turtle incarnation of Lord Vishnu ) took place. These days there is a temple called Kranteshwar Mandir, which is dedicated to lord Shiva. It is also believed that the head of Ghatotkacha (son of Bhima and the Rakshasi Hidimbi ) fell here after he died in the battle of Mahabharata . The Gahtku Mandir is the temple dedicated to Ghatotkacha . There is a famous temple called the Shani Mandir (or Manokamna Purn Mandir Kaula) in the village of Maurari

name: TRH Chaukori
description: Chaukori is a must visit destination to attain both spiritual and mental peace, away from the bustling crowd and noise. It offers the bliss one can derive from natural landscape.

name: TRH Dharchula
description: From Jauljibi one passes one passes through Kimkhola, Baluakot and Kalika, to reach the border township of Dharchula. It is an important camp along the Kailas- Mansarovar route. The region resembles a stove thus is known as Dharchula. The town is situated in the beautiful valley and is 90kms from the district head quarters, Pithoragarh. It is known for woollen products and is accessible round the year.

name: TRH Didihat
description: Didihat is at a distance of 54kms from Pithoragarh. The place is enriched with the natural beauty and lush green flora. Didihat is situated on the hill top plain of 'Digtarh' and river Charamgad or Bhadigad streaming below. Didihat is named after word ‘Dand’ which means a small hillrock. Mesmerising view of the peaks like Panchachuli and Trishul can be viewed from here. Nearby ten km from here, Narayan Swamy Ashram at Narayan Nager is worth visiting.
address: Oak Park House Mallital NainitalMain Market, Didihat, Distt: Pithoragarh (Uttarakhand) - 262551

name: Mahaashay TRH Dudhauli
description: Located about 15 km from Dwarahat, this pristine temple is highly revered by the locals. Owing to the colour of soil here, the temple is also called Mangalikhan. Mangal implying the planet Mars which is associated with the orange soil found here. The 350 steps leading to the temple are surrounded by majestic peaks and the melodious sounds of nature. The Dunagiri temple is also associated with the indian epic, Ramayan as it is said Hanuman ji dropped a piece of the sanjivinibuti at this place. A must visit for the positive vibrations and absolute peace and calm it offers.
address: Dwarahat Dunagiri Road, Dudhauli, Distt: Almora (Uttarakhand)

name: TRH Gangolihat
description: Gangolihat is an important religious center in the Kumaon region which is at a distance of 77kms from Pithoragarh. It is very well known for the HaatKalika temple. At a distance of 9kms is the PatalBhuvaneshwar temple complex with lime rocks inside it. These rocks have taken various attractive shapes due to the effect of water. It portrays the environment as a living being that breathes and feels.

name: TRH Jageshwar
description: 35kms from Almora, Jageshwar is believed to be the abode of the twelve Jyotirlings. It is situated in a beautiful narrow valley surrounded by magnificent Deodar trees. Jageshwar is the cluster of large and small temples and of the Swayambhu (jyotrilinga). Leaving the main road behind, one moves into the beautiful valley of Jata Ganga at Aartola and passes by the Daneshwar temple along the way, innumerable Deodar trees tower above the grand temple complex. The complex, consisting of 120 temples and hundreds of statues, is famous for its exquisite craftsmanship. The main temple in the complex is dedicated to Bal Jageshwar, or Shiva the child. There is another dedicated to VridhJageshwar, situated on the higher slopes.
address: KMVN TRH, Near Jageshwar Temple, Jageshwar. (Uttarakhand) - 263682

name: TRH Kausani (Trishul)
description: Kausani is a dream destination, the vantage point for a breathtaking view of the Nanda Devi mountain range, amidst dense pine forest. One can feel the proximity of the snowy Himalayan peaks Trishul, Panchchuli, Nanda Ghnti and Chaukhamba from here and immense yourself into the scenic grandeur. Mahatma Gandhi spent some time here, while he was writing the book ‘Anashakti Yoga’ a commentary on Bhagwat Gita. The ‘Anashakti Ashram’ was founded here by his disciple Sarla Ben (Katherine Heilemen). From an impressive height of 1,890mtrs the Himalayas can be seen in their towering glory. Below is the Gomti river rushing into the Katyuni valley. Kausani is also the birthplace of famous Hindi poet Sumitra Nandan Pant.

name: TRH Lohaghat
description: Lohaghat the scenic town in the Kumoan region of Uttarakhand is still an unspoilt beauty. It has a rich historical past. On the bank of river Lohawati, Lohaghat is a destination of historical and mythological significance. One can go for fishing and water sports activities from here to Pancheshwar. The sikh shrine MeethaReetha Sahib, enrouteNainital and Almora is another tourist attraction. In the nineteenth century, the British were so overwhelm by its beauty, that they proposed to develop it as summer capital of the then British empire. A city with a remarkable past, amidst natural abundance and a mystic aura of hill romance and new found resurgence, the whole area is an exquisite combination of natural beauty, historical importance and salubrious atmosphere.
address: KMVN TRH, Pancheshwar Road, Lohaghat, Distt: Champawat. (Uttarakhand) - 262524

name: TRH Mukteshwar
description: Mukteshwar, once a British cantonment, is located 52kms from Nainital. It offers some of the most magnificent views of the Himalayan peaks. The oldest town of the region Almora equidistant from Nainital and Mukteshwar is 60kms away. Steeped in Indian culture andtraditions, Swami Vivekanand recommended Almora as a great place to meditate.NearMukteshwar is a stone hole of Chauki Ki Jali, dedicated to Lord Shiva. Mukteshwar offers a spectacular view of the majestic Peaks of Adi Nampa of Nepal stretching upto the Chaukhamba peaks in Garhwal
address: KMVN TRH, Near Mahadev Temple, Mukteshwar. (Uttarakhand) - 263138

name: TRH Munsyari
description: Munsiyari is situated in Pithoragarh, the easternmost hill district of Uttarakhand, bordering Tibet, which is known as ‘Little Kashmir’. The region is paradise for nature lovers and adventurous souls. One can have the breathtaking view of the Himalayan peak, Panchchuli from here. Munsiyari is the base camp for the trekkers to Milam, Ralam glaciers and Nanda Devi peak. A fast developing centre for skiing and other winter sports. Munsiyari, when translated refers to a ‘place with snow’. Situated on the banks of Goriganga river, it is a vast growing tourist destination, Glacier enthusiasts, high altitude trekkers and nature lovers commonly use it as their hub or base camp.

The way to the cave temple is through a long narrow tunnel. Inside the cave, the limestone formations have taken shape of many Gods and Goddess of Hindu pantheon. The forms of Ganesha, Shesh Nag, Garurh, Shivling etc. are distinctly visible to the believers.
